concept.heading: Core Patterns
bullets: **Fast & Slow pointers:** Cycle detection, find middle
**Dummy head:** Simplifies edge cases when head might change
**Merge:** Compare heads, advance the smaller one

problems.title: Reverse Linked List
problems.keyInsight: Three pointers: prev, curr, next. Save next, reverse curr's pointer, advance all three.

code.python:
def reverseList(head):
    prev, curr = None, head
    while curr:
        nxt = curr.next   # save
        curr.next = prev  # reverse
        prev = curr       # advance prev
        curr = nxt        # advance curr
    return prev

problems.title: Reorder List
problems.keyInsight: 3 steps: (1) Find middle with slow/fast, (2) Reverse second half, (3) Merge alternating from both halves.

code.python:
def reorderList(head):
    # 1. Find middle
    slow, fast = head, head.next
    while fast and fast.next:
        slow = slow.next
        fast = fast.next.next
    
    # 2. Reverse second half
    second = slow.next
    slow.next = None
    prev = None
    while second:
        nxt = second.next
        second.next = prev
        prev = second
        second = nxt
    
    # 3. Merge alternating
    first, second = head, prev
    while second:
        tmp1, tmp2 = first.next, second.next
        first.next = second
        second.next = tmp1
        first, second = tmp1, tmp2

problems.title: Remove Nth Node From End of List
problems.keyInsight: Advance fast pointer n steps ahead. Then move both until fast hits end. Slow is now at the node before the one to remove.

problems.title: Copy List with Random Pointer
problems.keyInsight: Two passes: (1) Create all copied nodes, store old-to-new mapping, (2) Set next and random pointers using the map.

code.python:
def copyRandomList(head):
    old_to_new = {None: None}
    curr = head
    while curr:  # Pass 1: create nodes
        old_to_new[curr] = Node(curr.val)
        curr = curr.next
    curr = head
    while curr:  # Pass 2: set pointers
        old_to_new[curr].next = old_to_new[curr.next]
        old_to_new[curr].random = old_to_new[curr.random]
        curr = curr.next
    return old_to_new[head]

def addTwoNumbers(l1, l2):
    dummy = ListNode()
    curr = dummy
    carry = 0
    while l1 or l2 or carry:
        v1 = l1.val if l1 else 0
        v2 = l2.val if l2 else 0
        total = v1 + v2 + carry
        carry = total // 10
        curr.next = ListNode(total % 10)
        curr = curr.next
        l1 = l1.next if l1 else None
        l2 = l2.next if l2 else None
    return dummy.next

problems.title: Linked List Cycle
problems.keyInsight: If there's a cycle, fast (2 steps) will eventually meet slow (1 step). Like two runners on a circular track.

problems.title: Find the Duplicate Number
problems.keyInsight: Treat array as linked list: index i points to nums[i]. Duplicate creates a cycle. Use Floyd's to find cycle entry point.

code.python:
def findDuplicate(nums):
    slow = fast = 0
    while True:  # Phase 1: find intersection
        slow = nums[slow]
        fast = nums[nums[fast]]
        if slow == fast:
            break
    slow2 = 0  # Phase 2: find cycle entry
    while slow != slow2:
        slow = nums[slow]
        slow2 = nums[slow2]
    return slow

problems.title: LRU Cache
problems.keyInsight: HashMap gives O(1) lookup. Doubly linked list gives O(1) insert/delete. Most recently used at tail, LRU at head. On access, move to tail. On capacity overflow, remove head.

problems.title: Merge K Sorted Lists
problems.keyInsight: Merge lists pairwise like merge sort. K lists become K/2, then K/4... O(N log K) total.

problems.title: Reverse Nodes in K-Group
problems.keyInsight: For each group of k nodes: (1) Check if k nodes remain, (2) Reverse k nodes, (3) Connect reversed group to previous group's tail and next group's head.

code.python:
def reverseKGroup(head, k):
    dummy = ListNode(0, head)
    group_prev = dummy

    while True:
        kth = group_prev
        for _ in range(k):  # find kth node
            kth = kth.next
            if not kth:
                return dummy.next
        group_next = kth.next
        # Reverse group
        prev, curr = kth.next, group_prev.next
        for _ in range(k):
            nxt = curr.next
            curr.next = prev
            prev = curr
            curr = nxt
        tmp = group_prev.next  # first node (now last)
        group_prev.next = kth  # connect to reversed head
        group_prev = tmp       # move to end of reversed group
